Given that clarification, retain the current staff-led process. Do not replace it with the automated proposal: it reduces the primary outcome from 90% to 65%, so its time saving is strategically irrelevant.

Use automation only as a bounded validation candidate:

- Run it in shadow mode alongside the staff process, with no unreviewed submissions reaching clients.
- Test whether automation plus mandatory human review can match or improve the current 90% correctness rate.
- Also analyse the current process’s 10% failures; fixing those may improve the primary outcome more directly.
- Stop or redesign the automated route if it produces lower correctness after review. Consider adoption only when comparable evidence shows no quality sacrifice.

The recommendation changed because you resolved the decisive ambiguity: submission correctness outranks staff time.
